related_questions.question: What benefits do disabled veterans get in Colorado?

text_blocks.snippet: Colorado offers a range of benefits to disabled veterans, including property tax exemptions, state employment preferences, and recreational discounts. These benefits are often tied to the veteran's disability rating as determined by the US Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
snippet_highlighted_words: property tax exemptions, state employment preferences, and recreational discounts

list.title: Property Tax Exemption:
list.snippet: A property tax exemption is available for eligible disabled veterans on their primary residence, often with a percentage reduction based on the disability rating (e.g., 50% of the first $200,000 of actual value for 100% disabled veterans).

list.title: State Employment Preference:
list.snippet: Veterans with disabilities receive preference points in state employment examinations, with disabled veterans receiving 10 points and nondisabled veterans receiving 5 points.

list.title: Recreational Discounts:
list.snippet: Veterans with a Disabled Veterans License Plate receive free admission to state parks.

list.title: Hunting and Fishing Licenses:
list.snippet: Colorado offers free hunting and fishing licenses to certain disabled veterans.

list.title: Tuition Assistance:
list.snippet: Colorado National Guard members may qualify for state tuition assistance, potentially covering up to 100% of tuition at state-funded schools.
Eligibility for specific benefits may vary based on the veteran's disability rating, service history, and other factors.
The Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs (CDVA) provides assistance in navigating these benefits and can help veterans determine their eligibility and apply for them.
The Colorado Department of Military and Veterans Affairs has trained County Veterans Service Officers who can provide free assistance to veterans and their families.
The Denver VA Regional Benefit Office can also provide information and assistance with VA benefits, which often play a role in determining eligibility for state-level benefits.
